source_caption:
Christoph Waltz spent decades working in European television and theater long before Hollywood finally recognized him. For years, he appeared mostly in German and Austrian productions, often playing supporting roles in crime dramas and stage performances, building a reputation as a highly skilled but largely overlooked actor outside Europe.

Everything changed in 2009 when Quentin Tarantino cast him as Hans Landa in Inglourious Basterds. Tarantino later admitted the role was so difficult to cast that he feared the film might fail entirely if he couldn’t find the right actor. Waltz’s ability to switch effortlessly between languages, charm, humor, and menace made the character unforgettable almost instantly.

The performance completely transformed his career overnight. After spending decades relatively unknown to mainstream audiences, Waltz won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor and suddenly became one of the most sought-after actors in Hollywood. He later reunited with Tarantino for Django Unchained, winning a second Oscar for his role as Dr. King Schultz.
